extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants / prosecution counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for handling restriction requirements, traverses, elections, withdrawal, and rejoinder in U.S. patent prosecution (MPEP guidance tied to 37 CFR and statutes). Covers examiner actions, applicant replies, petition rights, and treatment of rejoined/nonelected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration request must include provisional election
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant disagrees with the requirement for restriction, he may request reconsideration and withdrawal or modification of the requirement, giving the reasons therefor. In requesting reconsideration the applicant must indicate a provisional election of one invention for prosecution, which invention shall be the one elected in the event the requirement becomes final. (37 CFR 1.143)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will reconsider the restriction when such a request is filed. If the requirement is repeated and made final, the examiner will act on the claims to the invention elected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse must be complete per 37 CFR 1.111(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The traverse to a requirement must be complete as required by 37 CFR 1.111(b): the reply must be reduced to writing which distinctly and specifically points out the supposed errors in the examiner’s action and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action; the reply must appear to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere broad allegation that the requirement is in error does not comply. Under this rule the applicant is required to specifically point out reasons on which he or she bases conclusions that a restriction is in error. Failure to do so makes the provisional election an election without traverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must elect even when requirement is traversed
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional election must be made even though the requirement be traversed. (37 CFR 1.143)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requirements for restriction should include form paragraph 8.22 advising that a complete reply includes (i) an election even though the requirement is traversed and (ii) identification of the claims encompassing the elected invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: To preserve right to petition, applicant must traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final requirement for restriction, the applicant may petition the Director to review the requirement (37 CFR 1.144). A petition will not be considered if reconsideration of the requirement was not requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the restriction requirement to preserve the right to petition; otherwise the election will be treated as without traverse and petition rights generally are not preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election treated as without traverse when reply incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reply does not distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the restriction requirement, the election shall be treated as an election without traverse. (Form paragraph 8.25.02)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.25.02 should be used to notify applicant when an election is treated as without traverse due to an incomplete reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of traversing only linking claim nonallowance
rubrics_metrics.description: An election of a single invention combined with a traverse of only the nonallowance of the linking claims is an agreement with the Office that restriction is proper if the linking claim is not allowable and improper if it is allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office allows the linking claim, it is bound to withdraw the restriction requirement and act on all linked inventions which depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of the allowable linking claim. But once all linking claims are canceled 37 CFR 1.144 would not apply since the record would be one of agreement as to the propriety of restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse contesting other relationships preserves petition rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the traverse is on the ground that there is some relationship (other than and in addition to the linking claim) that also prevents restriction, the merits of the requirement are contested and not admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restriction is made final in spite of such traverse, the right to petition is preserved even though all linking claims are canceled. When a final restriction requirement is contingent on the nonallowability of the linking claims, applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.144 without waiting for a final action on the linking claims, but not later than appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office generally does not permit shift to a different invention after election
rubrics_metrics.description: The general policy of the Office is not to permit the applicant to shift to claiming another invention after an election is once made and action given on the elected subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant cannot, as a matter of right, file an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims independent and distinct from the claims previously claimed and examined. When claims are presented which the examiner holds are drawn to an invention other than the one elected, they should be treated as outlined in MPEP § 821.03. For certain CPAs filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) that are continuations of a parent (not divisionals), an express election in the parent carries over to the CPA unless otherwise indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonelected claims withdrawn from further consideration (37 CFR 1.142(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims that the examiner holds as not being directed to the elected subject matter are withdrawn from further consideration by the examiner in accordance with 37 CFR 1.142(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should clearly set forth in the Office action the reasons why the claims withdrawn from consideration are not readable on the elected invention. Applicant may traverse the requirement pursuant to 37 CFR 1.143 and may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.144 if a final restriction is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: After election with traverse examiner must reconsider and respond; may make requirement final
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the initial requirement is traversed, it should be reconsidered; if upon reconsideration the examiner is still of the opinion that restriction is proper, it should be repeated and made final in the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should reply to the reasons or arguments advanced by applicant in the traverse. Form paragraph 8.25 (Answer to Arguments With Traverse) should be used to make a restriction requirement final, including a summary of applicant's grounds and why found unpersuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: If examiner withdraws restriction after reconsideration, must specify rejoined groups and act on merits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner, upon reconsideration, is of the opinion the requirement is improper in whole or in part, he or she should clearly state in the next Office action that the requirement for restriction is withdrawn in whole or in part, specify which groups have been rejoined, and give an action on the merits of all the claims directed to the elected invention and any invention rejoined with the elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs such as 8.45, 8.46, 8.50, etc., are used to notify applicant of rejoinings and the specific claims rejoined; the examiner must act on the merits of rejoined claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final reply must include cancellation of nonelected claims when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing a final action in an application where there has been a traversal of a requirement for restriction, the examiner should indicate in the Office action that a complete reply must include cancellation of the claims drawn to the nonelected invention, or other appropriate action (37 CFR 1.144).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.24 in FINAL rejections containing nonelected claims withdrawn with traverse. Failure to cancel such claims in the reply may be treated as authorization to cancel by examiner's amendment and pass the application to issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to act on nonelected claims when application is ready for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application is otherwise in condition for allowance and has not received a final action, the examiner should notify applicant of options and the requirement that claims directed to nonelected inventions be canceled or other steps taken; failure to take action will be treated as authorization to cancel the noted claims by Examiner’s Amendment and pass the case to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.03 (In Condition for Allowance, Non-elected Claims Withdrawn with Traverse) gives the ONE MONTH/THIRTY DAYS timeframe; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted in that context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims added after an Office action for a different invention treated under 37 CFR 1.145
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims added by amendment following action by the examiner to an invention other than previously claimed should be treated as indicated by 37 CFR 1.145.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.04 (Election by Original Presentation). An amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to the nonelected invention is nonresponsive; notify applicant with form paragraph 8.26 and give time to correct to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder eligibility requires dependence on all limitations of an allowable claim
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to be eligible for rejoinder, a claim to a nonelected invention must depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim. A withdrawn claim that does not require all the limitations of an allowable claim will not be rejoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where restriction was between product and process and the product invention was elected and found allowable, all claims to a non-elected process invention must depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim to be eligible for rejoinder. Applicant should amend nonelected claims during prosecution to require limitations of the elected invention to retain right to rejoinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoined claims must meet all patentability requirements (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, 112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejoined claims must be fully examined for patentability in accordance with 37 CFR 1.104; to be allowable, the rejoined claims must meet all criteria for patentability including the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103 and 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejoined claims are unpatentable (e.g., rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph), the provisions of MPEP § 706.07 govern whether the next Office action may be made final, particularly where the new ground of rejection was necessitated by applicant’s amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of restriction removes 35 U.S.C. 121 protection and may create double patenting risk
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of the withdrawal of the restriction requirement, the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 121 are no longer applicable. Any claim presented in a continuation or divisional application that is anticipated by, or rendered obvious over, claims of the parent application may be subject to a double patenting rejection when the restriction requirement is withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Ziegler and MPEP § 804.01. Examiner should advise applicant when rejoin occurs that continuation or divisional claims including limitations of an allowable claim may be subject to provisional statutory and/or nonstatutory double patenting rejections over the instant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and entry of amendments relating to rejoined claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presenting additional claims that depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim will be entered as a matter of right if presented prior to final rejection or allowance, whichever is earlier. Amendments submitted after final rejection are governed by 37 CFR 1.116; amendments after allowance are governed by 37 CFR 1.312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If nonelected claim(s) which depended from or required all the limitations of an allowable claim were canceled by applicant, they may be reinstated by timely amendment in reply to the action; upon entry such claims will be examined for patentability under 37 CFR 1.104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific form paragraphs to communicate election/traverse/rejoin actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP prescribes specific form paragraphs (e.g., 8.22, 8.25, 8.25.01, 8.25.02, 8.05, 8.03, 8.24, 8.04, 8.26, 8.45, 8.46, 8.49, 8.50) to be used in Office actions to acknowledge elections, traverses, withdrawals, rejoinings, and to instruct applicant on required next actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs include prescribed language for acknowledging election with/without traverse, explaining why claims are withdrawn, advising on cancellation deadlines, notifying of non-responsive amendments, and warning about double patenting consequences; examiners should use the appropriate form paragraph in each factual situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: When nonelected claims do not require all limitations of an allowable claim, explain why they remain withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: When no claims directed to the nonelected invention(s) depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim, the examiner should explain why all nonelected claims are withdrawn from further consideration (use form paragraph 8.49).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice should state that the restriction requirement is withdrawn as to any claim that requires all the limitations of an allowable claim and identify the claims that remain withdrawn and the reasons (e.g., they do not all require the limitations of the allowable linking/generic claim).
